codex.verification_method: 0.146.0 was exercised on the maintainer machine; 0.147.0 through 0.152.1 support was reviewed against the official OpenAI release deltas. .codex-version tracks 0.156.0 pending the next direct CLI validation. 0.150 adds native task references and Interrupt hooks; 0.151 adds optional-MCP discovery grace, extension-side MCP result interception, and stronger per-repository plugin catalog handling; 0.152 adds package-style MCP names, per-tool output_token_limit, long app-server shell-command timeouts, and makes update_plan opt-in. 0.152.1 is a Guardian policy fix. None requires a shared plugin-manifest migration. The manifest hooks field is NOT a 0.147.0 feature: 0.147.0 is portable agent plugins (catalog install), while plugin-manifest hooks were wired into the hook runtime by openai/codex PR #19705, merged 2026-04-28, roughly twenty releases earlier. core/capabilities/platforms.json briefly recorded codex hooks as since 0.147.0 on that confusion; the exact floor has never been established here, so the registry now claims none. 2026-09-21 correction (PR #183, objective codex-guard-fix): the same registry row's notes ended with 'Not the same shape as Claude hooks/hooks.json', and docs/user/install/codex.md's capability table said hooks.json 'does not port' to Codex. Both were false and are corrected. hooks/hooks.json DOES port: .codex-plugin/plugin.json points its hooks field at this repo's own file, manifest.rs:149-155 accepts the same HooksFile type the engine consumes, Codex's own test uses plugin_root.join('hooks/hooks.json'), the engine is named ClaudeHooksEngine, it sets CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT, exit-2 blocking semantics match, and core/src/tools/hook_names.rs:29-38 ships Claude tool-name matcher aliases deliberately. The narrower true statement is that coverage is PARTIAL: WorktreeCreate, WorktreeRemove, DirectoryAdded and Notification have no Codex equivalent and never fire. The same table's subagents row (native -> unknown) and MCP row (.codex/config.toml -> the manifest mcpServers field) were corrected in the same pass. All of it is source-derived from openai/codex main; no live codex binary was run, and that caveat travels with the claims. 2026-09-21 review (PR #158): reviewed_through and latest_known advanced 0.152.1 -> 0.155.1 against the official OpenAI release notes for rust-v0.153.0, rust-v0.154.0, rust-v0.155.0 and rust-v0.155.1; 0.155.1 was the newest stable tag at that time, 0.156.0 existing only as alpha prereleases; 0.156.0 went stable 2026-09-22 and is reviewed below. validated_against stays 0.146.0 - still no live codex binary was run, and that caveat travels with every claim below. None of the three releases requires a shared plugin, skill or manifest schema migration. Relevant to this repo: 0.153.0 gives the plugin CLI remote-marketplace list, install and remove, which is the install path docs/user/install/codex.md documents. 0.154.0 makes existing sessions pick up newly installed plugin tools and refresh skills AND hooks after an out-of-process plugin upgrade or rollback (openai/codex #42284, #42593, #42990) - this matters here because Codex records hook trust per content hash, so a refresh that changes hook content resets it to needing review; the untrusted-by-default gate documented in the install doc still applies after an upgrade. 0.154.0 also removes the deprecated `codex mcp-server` entry point, which this repo never referenced (MCP is declared through the plugin manifest's mcpServers field pointing at ./.mcp.json). 0.154.0 adds experimental native worktree support (--worktree, /worktree) and 0.155.0 adds worktree ownership detail plus confirmed deletion of clean managed worktrees; worktree isolation stays `emulated` in the registry because the skill still runs `git worktree` itself and the native feature is experimental and outside the plugin manifest - adopting it would be a Codex-specific surface, not a shared-hook change. 0.155.0 adds Touch ID user verification for MCP requests in local TUI sessions on supported Macs, and accurate expired-OAuth reporting with reconnect guidance; both are host capabilities needing no manifest change. 0.155.0 also adds configurable daemon update schedules, `codex app-server daemon update`, and saved-thread and active-goal recovery across daemon restarts. Approval and sandbox hardening across 0.154.0-0.155.0: startup no longer runs workspace-controlled PATH helpers before trust is established, the macOS sandbox blocks terminal input injection, Windows process escapes from restricted WSL sandboxes are blocked, and brokered shell snapshots are hardened against credential exposure. 0.155.1 is a single bug fix restoring `none` as the TUI reasoning-summary default for new local sessions (openai/codex #46467), fixing request rejection by providers that do not support reasoning summaries; explicit reasoning-summary settings remain respected. 2026-09-23 review: reviewed_through and latest_known advanced 0.155.1 -> 0.156.0 against the official release notes for rust-v0.156.0 (published 2026-09-22). validated_against stays 0.146.0; still no live codex binary. Nothing in it requires a plugin, skill or manifest migration. Two entries matter here: worktree support is now ENABLED BY DEFAULT, which retires the premise of the backlog item that declined native Codex worktrees as experimental in 0.154.0 (issue #180 E2 needs re-evaluating on its merits, not on staleness), and /usage now reports plugin and skill activity, adjacent to usage-capture and session-report. The remainder is TUI/voice/themes, sandbox isolation hardening (inbound Windows connections, privileged Linux/macOS sockets, writes through read-only macOS file handles) and MCP OAuth credential refresh on a 503 - none on the adapter surface.

capability_source_note: targets.<key>.capabilities and capability_gaps are DERIVED from the capability registry and must not be hand-edited. Regenerate with `bash scripts/check-platform-targets.sh . --sync-capabilities`; `scripts/check-feature-equivalence.sh` fails when they drift.
version_claims_note: `validated_against` is the version this repo was last exercised against on a live maintainer machine. `reviewed_through` is the newest upstream release whose notes have actually been read for adapter impact. They are different claims and they drift apart on purpose: reading release notes is cheap and should always be current, while a live run needs a maintainer at a machine. V1-04 fires on `reviewed_through < latest_known` -- nobody has looked at what shipped -- because that is the gap a contributor can actually close. It deliberately does not fire on a validated_against lag, which is bounded instead by `last_reviewed` and V1-05's 90-day budget. A target with no `reviewed_through` falls back to `validated_against`, so consumer repos that have not adopted the field score exactly as before.
